items.new: You will see that this mere painstaking burrower and grub-worm of a poor devil of a Sub-Sub seems to have gone through the long Vaticans and street-stalls of the earth, picking up whatever random allusions to whales he could find anywhere, in any book whatsoever, sacred or profane. So you must not, in every case at least, take the higgledy-piggledy whale statements in these extracts, however authentic, as genuine gospel cetology. Far from it. As for the ancient authors in general, and the poets who appear here as well, these extracts are valuable or entertaining only because they offer a glancing bird's-eye view of what has been said, thought, imagined, and sung about Leviathan, indiscriminately, by many nations and generations, including our own.

items.reason: narrator prose: full sentence-by-sentence modern rendering, thee/ye to you
items.new: So farewell, poor devil of a Sub-Sub, whose commentator I am. You belong to that hopeless, sallow tribe that no wine in this world will ever warm, and for whom even Pale Sherry would be too rosy-strong; but with whom one sometimes loves to sit, and feel poor-devilish too, and grow convivial over tears, and say to them bluntly, with full eyes and empty glasses, and in a sadness not altogether unpleasant — Give it up, Sub-Subs! For the more pains you take to please the world, the more thankless you will go forever! I wish I could clear out Hampton Court and the Tuileries for you! But gulp down your tears and hurry aloft to the royal-mast with your hearts; for your friends who have gone before are clearing out the seven-storied heavens, and making refugees of long-pampered Gabriel, Michael, and Raphael, in readiness for your coming. Here you strike only splintered hearts together — there, you shall strike unsplinterable glasses!
